feedback:
The revision closes most of the previous round's defects. Verified against the current text: D-029 gives every derived text result a run and a parent, so re-recognition provenance now works for the ordinary chain; D-030 replaces the untested claim that a truncated CAF can be finalized with a journal the application writes and fsyncs itself; D-031 lists a recovery transition for every stage the run machine names; D-032 replaces the single global revocation outcome with a capability-by-state matrix; D-026 removes the maximum-hold cap; D-033 puts retention, playback and export under one lease protocol; D-022 makes activation an immutable content-addressed install plus one transaction, records per-asset licences and notices as RESEARCH asks, and states that a smoke test is a capability check so a compatible import with no benchmark row activates and is labelled unmeasured, which is what the specification demands; D-035 names the product owner as approver with clause traceability; D-003 and D-028 move from a symbol scan RESEARCH rejects as evidence to a sandboxed service with the network entitlement withheld; D-020 and D-023 now make the runtime and diarizer choices on the evidence that exists and keep the measurements that would evaluate them explicitly unperformed. Those objections no longer apply.

The defects that remain are concrete and were checked against the proposal text.

1. Diarization exists in D-023 as model-bound work with its own results, and it exists nowhere else in the machine. The run kinds are dictation, import, reprocess_recognition and reprocess_text. The stages are arming, capturing, sealing, recognizing, refining, rewriting, delivering. results.kind is recognition, normalized, rewritten, translation, notes. So diarization has no run kind, no entry stage, no result kind, no cancellation entry in D-007 and no recovery row, and D-031's claim that every non-terminal state has an authoritative transition does not reach it. D-007 also has no cancellation entry for sealing. Meeting-note provenance has the matching hole: a note derives through a single derived_from_result_id, while its content depends on diarization output and on speaker assignments the user can edit, and the manifest pins neither. Renaming a speaker or re-running diarization can change how a saved note reads with no change to its recorded provenance, which is the failure D-006's snapshot rule exists to prevent.

2. D-023 depends on SpeakerKit exposing per-segment clustering distance and margin and on accessible centroid embeddings for cross-run identity matching. RESEARCH establishes the download flag, the model folder, the segmenter and embedder concurrency settings and the fact that the threshold is not calibrated. It does not establish the rest. The assumption entry records a basis for the calibration point only, and the open question is marked non-blocking with a fallback that answers calibration (unknown confidence plus manual assignment) and not embedding access, which is what carries edited names across a re-run. This is admissible as an unperformed experiment if the dependency and its structural fallback are recorded; as written the schema commits to evidence the cited source does not show is available.

3. Delivery confirmation is still unsound in a case that duplicates text. D-009 treats a change in value length or selected-text range as delivered and an absence of change as rejected, and an observed rejection is what unlocks synthesized typing. A paste that replaces a selection with equal-length text changes no length, so a target exposing only value length yields a false rejection and the ladder types the paragraph a second time. Two further inconsistencies sit next to it. D-008 says focus moving within the same application delivers into the current element, while D-009 acts on the latched element. The submit rule fires only when the path posted events, which excludes the preferred AXSelectedText rung, so the optional submission the specification asks for is unavailable on the path the design prefers. D-010's state set is pending, posted, posted_unconfirmed, held, failed, with no terminal success state, while recovery produces needs_review, which is not in the set; taken literally, the launch rule converts every historical posted attempt into a review item.

4. D-030's durability protocol does not state that the ALAC bytes are fsynced before the index entry naming them becomes durable, so recovery can rebuild a packet table over bytes that never reached disk. The index carries chunk sequence, packet count and byte offset, which is not enough to reconstruct a variable-packet ALAC packet table; per-packet sizes are needed. F3's only stated fallback is a shorter chunk period, which addresses tail-loss frequency and neither of these.

5. The process boundary is unassigned for diarization. The bundles are SpeechService, GenerationService, DecodeService and ModelDownloader, and DiarizerSpeakerKit is listed as an adapter target with no service. D-028 says inference runs in services denied the network, and RESEARCH specifically warns that this runtime's default initialization may download models, so the one component whose egress risk is documented is the one with no stated home. Scheduling has the same omission: D-004 admits at most one speech and one generation job and D-027 budgets one speech and one generation model, while D-023 adds segmenter and embedder models with their own concurrency. Relatedly, the capture sealer is placed in the batch lane with no exemption from admission, so a long import can starve the sealer that keeps the journal window near thirty seconds, and D-004's cancel-and-restart default restarts from a checkpoint whose fidelity is the property the descriptor has not yet established.

6. Runtime replacement does not have the bounded storage effect the specification requires. Garbage collection removes blobs with no installation row and no live lease, and History results permanently reference the installation that produced them, so no installation row is ever unreferenced and no weights are ever collectible. The evolution section's claim that a runtime's blobs can be released once nothing references them does not follow from D-022 as written. There is no state in which an installation stays attributable while its weights are discarded.

7. D-011's reconsideration condition degrades the preview to a waveform and a voice-activity indicator if the provisional pass proves expensive. The provisional live transcript is a named requirement, so that condition drops scope rather than adjusting a parameter.

8. Acceptance bases are partly missing. The fidelity rubric lists criteria with no scoring or rejection rule, and F1 has no recognition or latency condition attached to retaining the default pairing, only a memory-slope fallback. This is the specification's basis-for-acceptance clause, and it is separate from the model-evaluation-is-not-a-feature-gate rule, which the design honours correctly.

9. The proposal carries its own blocking open question on Developer ID against App Store distribution while D-003, D-009 and D-026 already assume the answer, and assumption three records the same item as a reversible assumption with a reconsideration condition. Those two treatments contradict each other. The specification's own required behaviours (a consuming session-level tap, push-to-talk key-up, setting selected text in another application) are not available under the App Store sandbox, so the design can settle this as a decision with that basis instead of leaving a blocking question standing.

Objections I judged overstated. The review's demand that automatic media resume be removed asks for more than the specification does: D-025 defaults resume to a user action, states in the interface that the app cannot confirm which application it addressed, and gates the opt-in path on posted-pause, same device, still idle and a ten-minute bound. That is a disclosed best-effort proxy for ownership, and removing the feature would drop behaviour the specification asks for. On the validator, the design already says in D-012 and in the purpose section that the checks are necessary conditions and bounds its claim to them, so the demand that it enforce instruction hierarchy absolutely is not satisfiable by any design; what is genuinely unresolved is narrower, namely that a sentence with no content-word support in the input is flagged with no stated consequence, so it is undefined whether that path fails, retries or passes. On the acceptance-threshold objection, F3 does carry a stated expectation and remedy and the diarization protocol correctly refuses to become a feature gate, so only the rubric scoring rule and the F1 retention conditions are missing.

Not stuck. Every confirmed defect is resolvable inside the design as written: a diarization run kind with its stage, cancellation and recovery rows and a notes result that pins its diarization and assignment inputs; a confirmation predicate keyed to the expected text at the expected location with an unconfirmed outcome whenever it is unavailable, plus a complete attempt-state table; one named target per focus outcome and submission tied to confirmed insertion; an explicit fsync and index-append order with per-packet metadata and a structural F3 fallback that retains chunks until a valid sealed artifact is durable; a named service for diarization with its models in the admission and residency accounting; an installation state that keeps identity and notices while releasing weights; a preview fallback that still shows provisional text; scoring rules for the rubric; and promotion of the distribution question to a decision on the basis the specification itself supplies. The SpeakerKit capability question needs an experiment, but the specification permits an unperformed experiment recorded with its fallback, so it does not force a stuck verdict.

Check mapping. requirements is false because Meetings lacks a lifecycle for the diarization it now ships, Models breaks the bounded-storage-on-runtime-replacement clause, Recording display's reconsideration condition would drop the required provisional transcript, and Text delivery's submit rule disables the requested modifier submission on the preferred path. architecture is false for the unassigned diarization service, the missing diarization lane and residency accounting, the sealer's placement under batch admission, and the latched-against-current element conflict between D-008 and D-009. alternatives is true: every decision weighs options that were genuinely available with costs stated, including the newly argued D-020 and D-023 and the rejected channel-only-meetings option. data_lifecycle is false for the diarization and speaker-assignment gap in the provenance graph, the incomplete journal ordering and packet metadata, the unbounded model blob retention, and the incomplete delivery_attempts state set. failures is false for the length-based paste confirmation, the launch rule over needs_review, the missing cancellation entries for sealing and diarization, and the undefined consequence of a flagged sentence. maintainability is false because the evolution section's storage-release claim does not follow from the garbage-collection rule and because a reconsideration condition is used to drop a named requirement. verification is false because the fidelity rubric has no pass rule, F1 has no retention condition beyond memory, F3's fallback does not cover a reconstruction failure, and no suite can assert diarization cancellation or recovery while those states do not exist. unresolved_decisions is false because a self-declared blocking question stands against an architecture that already assumes its answer, and because the diarization service placement, the sealer's admission status, the delivery target on same-application focus change, the flagged-sentence outcome, and the priority field D-014 tiebreaks on are all left to whichever implementation task reaches them first.
